intro_title_en: Start with no Chinese: script and chapter preparation
intro_en: Start here with no Chinese assumed. Read the script preparation for your next chapter before its story. If you arrived through a direct chapter link, use How to read to return here first. The preparation is additional to the chapter, its Pensa and its workbook. You can study it in several short sittings.

Read the Chinese horizontally from left to right. A square written form is a character; a word can contain one or more characters. The story has no spaces between its ordinary words. Punctuation separates clauses and speech. Learn the traditional forms shown here; no simplified-script knowledge is assumed.

Roman letters give modern Mandarin citation readings, not reconstructed ancient sounds. A tone mark belongs to the syllable: ā is high and level, á rises, ǎ dips and rises in isolation, à falls. An unmarked syllable is light. Citation tones may change in connected speech. Keep your tongue as for “ee” and round your lips for ü. Xī'ān has two syllables, xī plus ān; xiān is one syllable. You will answer in Chinese characters, without tone-typing or audio tasks.

For typed answers, a traditional-Chinese pinyin input method lets you type the supplied roman reading without tone marks, then choose the exact written character from its candidates. Compare shapes carefully. While learning input, you can copy a form from the visible reference. Pinyin is a lookup aid; its letters do not all have English sound values, and fluent Mandarin pronunciation is not a prerequisite for following these scenes.

A subject is the person or thing a sentence says something about. In the worked examples a person performs an action on a book: the book is the object directly related to that action. Verbs do not take English-style person or tense endings. No word for “a” or “the” is needed in these examples.

Worked contrast: 橋在水中，人在岸。橋有路，人在岸，視水。安在岸，待客。 — A bridge is in the water while a person is on the bank. The bridge has a path; the person looks at the water from the bank. An waits for the guest on the bank.

近 and 遠 can describe a named place without an extra verb meaning “is”: 橋近，山遠。 — The bridge is near; the mountain is far away. Worked contrast: 人有書，書在岸。人視山，止。橋近，安至橋。 — A person has a book, which is on the bank. The person looks at the mountain and stops. The bridge is near and An reaches it. Nearness and distance depend on the people’s current viewpoint, not fixed sizes.

遲 describes lateness: 安遲，寧待安。 — An is late and Ning waits for him. This is not a newly licensed word for walking slowly. Worked continuation: 寧在橋，客在岸。客待安，安至岸。寧視安，立。 — Ning is at a bridge and the guest on a bank. The guest waits for An, who reaches the bank; Ning looks at An and stands.

渡川 — dù chuān — cross the river; the river is the object of 渡. A changed bank after the action makes the result explicit: 安渡川，至東岸。寧在東岸，待安。客在西岸，視川。 — An crosses the river and reaches the east bank, where Ning waits for him. A guest is on the west bank looking at the river. Do not infer an unmentioned crossing merely from a later person’s position.

In 家遠, “the household is far away,” 家 refers to the family household back at home. The spatial context supplies its location; it does not turn 家 into a new general word for a building. Worked scene: 家遠，山近。安在岸，視山。寧在橋，待安。客持紙，安立。 — The household is far away and the mountain near. An looks at the mountain from the bank, Ning waits at the bridge, and the guest holds paper while An stands. Keep the old household distinct from a newly encountered gate.

主，誰也？安不知主。安有書，寧無書。客持紙，紙有姓。安視紙，寧視書。 — The owner—who is it? An does not know the owner. 誰 is the unknown identity in the nominal predicate, followed by the already known 也. 不 denies 知, not the noun 主. Having or holding an object does not identify its owner.

書在何處？書在門外。安持書，寧持燈。人在門內，門閉。客在門外，持紙。 — Where is the book? It is outside the gate. 在 remains the location predicate; 何處 is what place. This is not an interrogative moved before a preposition. Only this where family is practised here; broad how/why and embedded know-who questions wait.

人問。安答。安呼寧，寧應。安視書，寧視紙。客持帙，帙有字。紙有姓。 — A person asks; An answers. 問 and 答 frame separate direct quotations, not a new embedded-question construction. Contrast a call answered by 應. An answer may report uncertainty rather than supply a name.

寧識半字，寧不知主。安視破葉，客視帙字。安持書，寧持燈。客持紙，紙有姓。 — Ning recognises the damaged identifying mark, but does not know the owner. 識 here means recognising that particular half-character or wrapper mark; it does not assert reading arbitrary writing. 知 has the direct object 主, the owner whose identity is unknown.

人指破葉，安視半字。寧持燈，燈明。客持紙，紙有姓。安視帙，帙有字。 — The person points to the damaged leaf; An looks at the half-character. 指 takes the pointed-to object directly. No finger/body noun sense or abstract general reference system is introduced.

誰假燈？寧假燈。人持燈，寧取燈。寧持燈，安持書。客持紙，視姓。 — Who will borrow the lamp? Ning offers to borrow it, and its current holder passes it to her. With a prospective offer and willing handoff, 假 is borrowing/on loan, not lending or being fake. Compare an unexplained taking: custody alone does not establish a loan. The present holder need not be its ultimate owner.

卷全，書不全。卷有全葉，書有破葉。安視全葉，寧視半字。客持紙，紙有姓。 — The fascicle is complete; the book is incomplete. 全 is the already taught whole/complete quality, now predicated and denied with 不. Comparing physical completeness does not prove that two volumes contain the same work or identify an owner.

一半 — yī bàn — one half. 一 is one and 半 is half; here the pair is a substantive, something that can stand as a subject. Practise this expression with the named complementary halves before learning wider quantity patterns. Worked contrast: 安持書，寧持燈。書有破葉，卷有全葉。安視書，寧視卷。 — Track the two distinct objects; incompleteness alone does not show how much is missing.

人指書。人：「書不全。一半在門內，一半在何處？」安視人，寧視書。客持紙，視人。 — The reader points to the book and assesses it: “The book is incomplete. One half is inside the gate; where is the other half?” The paired one-half statements contrast a present part with its unlocated complement. This is his assessment and open question, not narrator arithmetic established merely by a damaged leaf. Try identifying which half is explicitly located and which is being asked about, before checking: first present, second unlocated.

葉在家，家遠。父持二葉，母持小書。先生持紙，紙有「安」字。安視書，寧持燈。 — The leaves are at the household back home; that home is far away. 家 refers to the known family home. Reporting that the leaves are there does not transport them into the present scene or turn 家 into a general new building sense.

人開門。人呼安，安應。安持書入門。寧持燈，客持紙。門內有火，火明。 — The person opens the gate, calls An, and An responds and enters holding the book. This sequence supplies a pragmatic invitation; 呼 itself still means call. Do not silently read a general word for permit into it. Each person’s movement is stated separately.

Chapter 7 — Read the dependency-ordered cards, then try all four retrieval packets and the worked reference contrasts before the story. These are separate miniature incidents, not new story facts. The earlier script and citation-reading policy continues. No picture supplies meaning.
乾 — gān — dry.
紙乾，書不乾。安持紙，寧持書。客持燈，燈明。安視紙，寧視書。門閉，人在門內。 — The sheet is dry and the book is not dry. The negative does not by itself mean completely wet.
先 — xiān — first; earlier.
安先視書。安閉書，取紙。寧持卷，客持燈。安視紙，寧視卷。紙有姓，卷有字。 — An first looks at the book, then closes it and takes a sheet. Practise first before the inspection verb 視 here, not a new later/after word.
束 — shù — bundle.

卷有帙。人持束，束有卷。寧視帙，安視卷。客持紙，紙有姓。人閉卷，寧持燈。 — A fascicle has a wrapper. The wrapped item is named a bundle and contains the fascicle. This is this particular assembled object; a fascicle without wrapping is not automatically a bundle. The word here is a noun, not bind.
兩 — liǎng — two (in the taught bundle count, liǎng).

人持兩束。束有卷，卷有帙。安視卷，寧視帙。客持紙，紙有姓。安持燈，燈明。 — The person holds two bundles. 兩 means two, without a natural-pair requirement. Practise only the finite count with bundles; it does not establish a general classifier system.
別 — bié — distinguish.

安別兩束。卷有帙，書有帙。帙同，書異。寧視卷，客持書。安持燈，燈明。 — An distinguishes the two bundles. Their covers match in outward appearance, while the contents differ. Matching covers are not the same physical cover or proof of identical books. Distinguish is not leave or a new word for other.
印 — yìn — mark; seal impression (noun on the wrapper here).
帙有印，紙有姓。安視印，寧視姓。客持紙，紙乾。安持卷，寧持燈。門閉，人在門內。 — The wrapper has a mark or seal impression, the sheet a surname. The mark is not a supplied readable name, a stamping action or proof of ownership.
左 — zuǒ — left.

書在左，卷在門內。安視書，寧持卷。客持紙，紙有姓。安持燈，燈明。門閉，人待安。 — The book is on the left, from An’s fixed viewing position in this miniature. A named person and observed object anchor the side; do not silently infer someone’s left hand.
右 — yòu — right.

卷在右，書在左。安視卷，寧視書。客持紙，紙有姓。安持燈，燈明。門閉，人在門內。 — The fascicle is on the right and book on the left, from the same fixed observer. These two side labels are the bounded locations used here, not arbitrary new spatial compounds.
此 — cǐ — this (demonstrative).
安指卷。卷有帙。此束有卷。寧持書，客持紙。安視此束，寧視紙。燈明，門閉，人在門內。 — An points to the wrapped fascicle: this bundle contains the fascicle. Put this before its named noun; the pointer establishes the selected reference.
彼 — bǐ — that (demonstrative).

安指卷。此束有卷，彼束有書。寧持彼束，客持紙。安持燈，視卷。門閉，人在門內。 — An selects the fascicle bundle as this; the contrasted book bundle is that. This and that do not permanently mean left and right, or belong to one particular book.
是 — shì — this (demonstrative, not modern copula).
是束有卷。安指卷，寧視帙。人持此束，客持彼束。客持紙，紙乾。燈明，門閉。 — This bundle contains the fascicle. Before the noun, this is the demonstrative reading, not the modern linking verb is or an answer meaning yes.
濕 — shī — wet.

帙有水，帙濕。紙乾，書不濕。安視帙，寧持書。客持紙，紙有姓。門閉，人在門內。 — The wrapper has water on it and is wet. The sheet is dry and the book is not wet. These are separate practice objects; which story object will be wet is not stated here.
誤 — wù — mistake (noun with has/knows here).
寧有誤，安知誤。寧視卷，客持書。安指印，寧視印。卷有帙，紙有姓。安持燈，燈明。 — Ning has made a mistake and An knows the error. Keep mistake a noun in has/knows frames; no new verb impede or miss is taught.

Pointing and attention: 安指此束，寧視彼束。此束有卷，彼束有書。人呼寧，寧應。安持燈，客持紙。 — An points to this bundle but Ning looks at that one. The reference remains fixed in the narration while attention changes. A mistaken character’s claim is not a narrator-certified fact.

Keep the viewpoint fixed for sides: 此束在左，彼束在右。寧持此束，客持彼束。寧在左，客在右。安視兩束，人在門內。 — The first bundle is on the left and the other on the right from An’s position; later the holders occupy those sides. There is no new left-hand/right-hand expression.

Each speaker’s point can select this: 寧指卷。寧：「此束有印。」客指書。客：「此束無印。」安視兩束，門閉。 — Ning points to the fascicle bundle and says this has a mark; the guest points to his book bundle and says this has no mark. The same demonstrative selects different objects because the speakers and explicit pointing change. It is not a contradiction or a permanent object name.

An unanswered question can matter: 寧問。客不答，持紙。人呼寧，寧應。寧視彼束，不別兩束。安持燈，客視紙。 — Ning asks, but the guest does not answer and holds the sheet. The reader calls her; she responds and looks at the other bundle without distinguishing them. 不答 denies answering, not the existence of a guest.

Wetness is a new problem after identity is corrected: 寧識印，寧不知主。寧持此束，帙有水。人開帙，開卷。人讀卷，止。客持紙，紙乾。 — A recognised mark identifies which wrapped object was lent, not its ultimate owner. Finding water and stopping reading motivate the next action; moving or opening a wet object does not instantly dry it.

Chapter 8 — 上 shàng, upper position/on/above; 下 xià, lower position/below. Study the dependency-ordered cards and all four retrieval packets before reading. The new spatial expressions combine a named object with a following position word. These practice incidents are separate from the continuing story. Traditional characters and Mandarin citation readings remain unchanged; no picture supplies meaning.

人持卷，安持燈。客持書，紙有姓。寧待人。門閉，人在門內。卷濕，帙有印。 — Before the new room and shelf words, retrieve the actual earlier ending: the reader has the wet marked fascicle, An the lamp, the guest his book and surname sheet; Ning waits. No ownership or distant-household transfer is implied.
屋 — wū — house; room.

人在屋內，持書。寧在門外，安持燈。屋內有火，火明。客持紙，紙有姓。人視紙，寧待安。 — The person is in the house/room. In the story this names the current near-gate reading interior, not the family household far away or a new roof noun. No unmentioned journey brings the family here.
架 — jià — shelf.

屋有架，架小。安持書，寧持燈。客持紙，紙有姓。人視書，安視紙。門閉，人在屋內。 — The room has a shelf; the shelf is small. It is a small free-standing shelf with accessible front and back in these incidents. Small is an inherited physical quality predicate.
上 — shàng — above; on.

卷在架上，紙在屋內。安視卷，寧持燈。客持書，書有帙。人持紙，紙有姓。門閉，人在屋內。 — The fascicle is on the shelf. Put the named shelf first, then the upper-position word: shelf + upper side. 上 here is a location, not climb or put up. 屋內 similarly names the inside of the current room, extending the earlier inside-gate formation through this spatial pattern.
下 — xià — below; lower position, selected as a location here.

架下有水，架上無水。葉在下，葉濕。安持卷，寧視葉。客持紙，紙乾。安持燈，門閉。 — There is water below the shelf, none on top. A leaf is in the lower position within the open fascicle; it is wet. A lower leaf can later be on top of the shelf when the whole fascicle is moved: internal page order and position relative to the shelf are different relationships. 下 remains a location, not a new action go down.
前 — qián — in front.

安至架前，寧持卷。紙在門前，門閉。安持燈，寧視書。客持紙，紙有姓。架上有卷，屋內有火。 — An reaches the space in front of the shelf. The named object precedes its front-position word. For the shelf the front faces An; for this house door the front is the outside approach. A location phrase can name the destination after the known reach verb.
後 — hòu — behind, the spatial use here; temporal after needs later preparation.

寧在架後，安在架前。人在門後，門閉。寧持卷，客持紙。安持燈，燈明。架上有書，紙乾。 — Ning is behind the shelf; An is in front. The person is behind the door, on its interior side in this scene. 後 here is behind; its different temporal after application still needs later preparation.
間 — jiān — between; among.

燈在兩束間。此束在左，彼束在右。安持燈，寧持卷。客持書，紙有姓。人視印，寧視帙。 — The lamp is between the two bundles. Put the named pair before between. The citation reading here is jiān. The two-bundle count is the earlier finite expression, not a general numeral system.
雨 — yǔ — rain.
門外有雨，人在屋內。安持燈，寧持卷。客持紙，紙乾。門閉，人在門後。寧待人，架上有書。 — There is rain outside; the person is inside. Rain is a noun with yǔ citation reading.
漏 — lòu — leak.

屋漏，水入屋。人持卷，寧視水。架下有水，架上無水。安持燈，客持紙。門閉，人在屋內。 — The building leaks and water enters the room. 漏 describes physical seepage here. 屋 names the room/building, not an added word roof. The old enter action now has water as its subject; no cause or direction complement is added.
移 — yí — move something.

安移燈。燈在架上。寧移卷。卷在架下。客持紙，紙乾。安視卷，寧視帙。門閉，人在屋內。 — An moves the lamp; its resulting location is stated separately. Ning moves the fascicle, with its location again separate. 移 takes the moved object directly; no unstudied put verb or complex goal complement is assumed.
壞 — huài — be damaged.

帙壞，卷不壞。安視帙，寧持卷。客持紙，紙不壞。架上有燈，架下有水。門閉，人在屋內。 — The wrapper is damaged, the fascicle is not. The sheet is not damaged. Damaged need not mean destroyed, and wet need not by itself mean damaged. No object instantly repairs itself.
存 — cún — preserve.

寧存卷，安存葉。卷在架上，架下有水。客存紙，紙在帙中。安持燈，燈在手。門閉，人在屋內。 — Ning preserves the fascicle and An helps preserve the leaves through the changed arrangement. The guest preserves his sheet by enclosing it. 存 is preserve/retain the material from further harm, not can contain, be dry or a guarantee of permanent safety.

母視箱。箱在門前。父持書，子持卷。門開，人在屋內。母移箱，子取紙。 — A chest is a container, not a book wrapper. These miniature incidents do not move the absent family into the continuing story.

Chapter 10 — 吾 wú means I, the current speaker; 汝 rǔ means you, one named addressee. Study the dependency-ordered cards and all four retrieval packets before reading. 人持帙，帙濕。卷在架上，卷濕。客持燈，持紙。書在架下，紙不在帙中。小箱空，扣壞。 — Retrieve the actual ending: the reader has his wet marked wrapper, his wet opened fascicle is on the dry-room shelf, the guest holds lamp and removed surname sheet, and his encased dry book rests below the shelf. The small clasp’s damage was discovered, with no proven time or culprit. The absent teacher has not yet arrived.
來 — lái — come.

師來，至門前。母開門，師入屋。子在屋內，父持書。母閉門，師視紙。子持卷，紙乾。 — The teacher comes and reaches the door. Come is movement toward the current speaker or scene, distinct from 去 go away. An explicit arrival is needed before an absent teacher can know the current events.
吾 — wú — I, the current speaker; my words in the taught finite expression.

師：吾持書。子：吾持紙。師在門前，子在屋內。母持卷，父視字。書乾，紙乾。子視書。 — The teacher’s I refers to the teacher; the child’s I to the child. The same form changes reference with the named speaker. In these examples it is a subject before its action, not a postverbal object.
告 — gào — tell; inform.

師告子。師：書在架上。子告母。子：紙在帙中。父持卷，母視紙。子取書，門開。 — Tell or inform the named recipient. The message follows as a separate attributed quotation; this is not a new recipient-plus-content double object or an embedded reporting clause.
汝 — rǔ — you, one explicitly identified addressee; your words in the taught finite expression.

師告子。師：汝持書。母告子。母：汝取紙。子持書，取紙。父在門前，師持卷。 — Each adult addresses the single named child. You does not silently include everyone present. The child addresses an adult teacher as 先生, not with this direct downward or familiar form. The recipient names and English labels identify the role before the clause.
信 — xìn — trust the named person or believe the identified words; not be trustworthy here.

母信子，子信先生。子持書，母持紙。父在門前，師在屋內。紙乾，卷濕。子視葉，母視字。 — The mother trusts the child; the child trusts the teacher. Later the named words, including the finite my-words and your-words expressions, can be the object of belief. Trust does not make every inference true. The first-person pronoun is not a positive postverbal object in this chapter.
言 — yán — words or an identified statement, noun here; not a new say-verb frame.

師告子。師：箱大。子視箱，箱大。子信此言。母持紙，父視字。子在門前，母在屋內。 — Words, or the identified statement: here the teacher’s assertion that the chest is large. The child believes this statement. 此言 points to that explicit speech, not an unidentified book title. This card uses the noun, not the separate say-verb use.
真 — zhēn — true.

箱大。師：箱大。此言真。母：箱小。此言不真。子視箱，父持書。母持紙，紙乾。 — The shown chest is large. The first statement is true; the second is not true of that scene. Evaluate the identified statement, not someone’s moral worth. A speaker’s claim that words are true remains that speaker’s claim until evidence supports it.
尋 — xún — seek.

子尋書，母尋紙。書在架上，紙在帙中。子見書，母見紙。父持卷，師在門前。箱空，門開。 — Seek or look for the named object or person. Searching is not itself finding, borrowing or owning. A later observation may resolve the search, but the verb alone does not promise success.
敢 — gǎn — courteous asking in 敢問, may I ask; not daring before arbitrary actions.

師持卷，子在門前。子：吾敢問：卷在何處？師：卷在架上。門開，母持紙。父視書。 — The child courteously asks may I ask, then gives the actual question. Only 敢問 is selected here, not an unrestricted dare construction. The teacher’s answer supplies the sought location.
諾 — nuò — assent to the immediately identifiable proposal, not an unqualified promise.

子：吾假書。師：諾。子取書，師持紙。母在屋內，父在門前。書乾，紙在帙中。 — Assent to the child’s immediately preceding borrowing proposal. The child may now take the offered book. The scope is that proposal; assent to inspection would not itself permit a later person to take the book away.
請 — qǐng — request the named object, or request permission for the speaker’s own inspection.

子：請書。師：諾。子取書，母持紙。父在門前，紙在帙中。子：請視書。師：諾。子視書，師持紙。 — The child requests the book, then requests permission for the child’s own inspection. 請視書 here means please allow me to inspect the book, not a command asking the teacher to inspect it. The named speaker is the requested inspector; the adult gives assent.

A question can name its sought person as the object: 子：吾敢問：先生見誰？師：吾見安。安持書，母持紙。父在門前，子視書。 — Who is the object of see in whom does the teacher see. The answer names An as that object. No embedded clause saying see someone do something is added; seeing a person and that person’s holding a book are separate statements.

The first outside return: retain this scope throughout the report and correction: 客還大書，安取大書。寧在門內，坐。安來，寧取大書。門閉，書在屋內。 — This recalls the first outside return in chapter 1: the visitor gave the large book back to An outside the original doorway. Ning was inside, then took it after An came back. She later handled and returned it again. Do not turn the correction into Ning never took the book. These verbs do not inflect for past time; the explicitly identified occasion supplies their reference.

Different knowledge about the two occasions: 安：吾在門外，取大書。寧：吾在門內，坐。先生：吾見寧，寧持大書。母持紙，父視字。 — An reports his own outside recovery; Ning confirms her own indoor position. The teacher has seen Ning holding the book later, when he arrived at the household in chapter 3. That later observation does not establish her participation in the earlier outside handoff. Keep the two occasions distinct. In the chapter’s quoted discussion, the teacher’s later admission that he did not see either child concerns that first outside recovery, not his whole history with them.

Only the actual participant can confirm his own handoff: 安：客還大書，吾取大書。師：吾問客。寧持書，安在門前。人持燈，紙在帙中。 — The visitor participated in the outside return; the teacher needs his actual account. The visitor has not yet supplied that decisive testimony. Ning’s own indoor testimony does not make her an eyewitness to the outside handoff, and the visitor’s outside presence would not independently prove everything Ning did indoors.

Separate the inspection and the onward loan: 師：吾假書。客：諾。師取書，開帙。師還書，客取書。寧：吾假書，假紙。客：諾。寧取書。 — First the teacher requests and receives a temporary inspection loan, opens the case before contents access, and returns it to the guest. A separate request and assent authorize Ning’s continuing loan of the book and enclosed surname sheet. Nothing here proves ultimate ownership. The guest’s earlier inspection permission alone would not authorize an unspecified child to take it onward.

Close the present scene without importing household objects: 客還燈，人取燈。安開門，客出門。安閉門，還。寧持書，紙在帙中。人持帙，持燈。 — The lamp returns to the near-gate reader before the visitor leaves. An opens and closes the rain-door because the reader now holds both the lamp and wet marked wrapper. Ning keeps the separately loaned dry book and enclosed sheet. The wet opened fascicle remains on the dry-room shelf. The teacher’s original fascicle and the distant household’s old loose leaves are different objects.

Identified words before action: 父：「汝尋紙。」子行此言，尋紙。母持卷，紙在帙中。父視子，子持紙。 — The father addresses one child. The child carries out those particular words by seeking the paper. The act-on reading has an identified instruction and an actual consequential action; it is not walking or an unmotivated moral maxim.

Old travel comparison: 行 — xíng — go; travel, already taught in chapter1. The graph and citation reading are shared, but travel occurrences do not teach the new act-on sense. This comparison does not introduce the separate later conduct noun.
乃 — nǎi — then; only then.

父閉書，乃開門。母持紙，子在屋內。父出門，母視門。書在帙中，紙在架上。 — Only after the explicitly stated closure does the father open the door. Put only-then before the selected action. No new past tense, copula or unannounced twice sense is supplied.
奔 — bēn — run; rush.

母開門，出門，閉門，奔至川。父在屋內，持紙。門外有雨。母至岸，止。 — The same named mother opens, goes out, closes and runs to the river. Longer serial actions retain their actor; a changed actor is named. Running and a destination reached through the known reach verb are explicit. Running does not prove criminal flight.
步 — bù — step; walk.

父步至橋，母奔至橋。父持書，母無書。父止，母視川。書在帙中，紙在帙中。 — The father walks; the mother runs. Walking is a selected verb here, not a new unit of distance. The carrier’s different pace can matter without a modern classifier or speed adjective.
行 — xíng — act on; put into practice.

父：「汝尋卷。汝行吾言。」子視父，取帙，尋卷。卷在屋內，父持紙。 — Within the father’s quotation my words refers to his immediately stated instruction. Act on my words differs from travel. The child’s actual seeking supplies its application; general teacher-words genitives are not licensed.
負 — fù — carry on the back.

母開帙，視書，視紙，閉帙，負書，持帙。書在帙中，紙在帙中。父步，母步。 — Back-carry the whole closed case containing book and sheet, keeping a handhold on the case against the back. The holding action is explicit. No unmentioned strap, tying action or free hands are assumed. A closed protective case can become wet; it is not waterproof.
返 — fǎn — return back.

父在屋內，持紙。父出門，至川，視水，返，至屋前。母在屋內，待父。 — Return has an earlier place and an on-page goal. This father returns to the room just established; it is not an unseen trip to a distant family home. At the story’s end An returns toward the near refuge.
追 — zhuī — follow in pursuit.

父追子，母持書。子奔，父奔；母步，持書。父至川，止。母至川，視父。 — Pursue the named child; the mother holds the book. Pursuit does not prove theft. Name the person, rather than using a later object pronoun. Distinguish following in pursuit from simply seeing.
速 — sù — quickly.

父速返，至門前。母持紙，待父。子速追父，母視子。子速至川，父在岸。 — Quickly precedes the selected return, pursuit or reaching action. It does not mean a fast person or give an ability complement. The named actor remains recoverable throughout each short chain.
隨 — suí — follow.

子隨母，父隨子。母持書，步至門前。子在屋內，父在門外。母止，子乃來。 — Each following verb has its own named subject and named person followed. Restore the subject whenever the role changes. Later absence of following need not mean intentional disobedience.

When following fails: 父：「汝隨安。」子至路，視水，止。子不行此言，不隨安。紙在帙中，子持帙。 — The identified instruction is to follow An. Water and the protected load prevent that action in this incident. Negative act-on-words is still the new semantic reading; this is not a judgment of character or a new cannot modal.

Narrator and witness: 日出，岸明。客在西岸，步。師在屋內，視卷。安見客。客在岸。 — The sun rises; illumination does not imply rain has stopped. A narrator can show Guest outside and Teacher inside with each actor explicitly restored. That does not give Teacher Guest’s route. The later separate seeing and location statements give An a real sighting without an embedded seeing-action construction.

Report scope: 安告先生。安：「吾見客。客在西岸。吾言真。」師：「吾信汝言。」 — An reports his own last sighting. His location statement recounts that sighting, not guaranteed continuing whereabouts. Teacher’s trust is attributed belief, not independent eyewitness knowledge. The guest is sought to give his own account of the chapter1 outside handoff, not to prove every indoor act.

Two physical routes: 路有水。此路在北，彼路在南。安至兩路間，視此路，視彼路。山在南，路在山前。 — These are two branches on the familiar west side of the river, not two unmentioned crossings. Between follows the named pair. The mountain-front area is its near/northern face as viewed from the junction. Ning takes the southern branch; An searches the near west-bank/northern approach. Neither child inherits the narrator’s unseen view.

Keep the referents separate: 寧持此帙，人持彼帙。此帙乾，彼帙濕。兩帙異，印在彼帙上。寧：「是帙乾。」 — The guest’s borrowed case stays with Ning; the wet marked wrapper stays with Reader. This is a demonstrative before a studied case noun, never a modern copula. A mark is not a decoded owner-name. The reader’s wet fascicle remains on the dry-room shelf under Teacher’s attention.

Return base: 師：「吾在此屋，視卷。安、寧返至此屋。」 — Teacher names the near refuge as the return point before the children leave. This is not their distant family home. The final return without Ning sets up12; no boat, ferry, ultimate owner or household transfer is invented.
